previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with hematuria and chills, consistent with a urinary tract infection, in the setting of a chronic indwelling Foley catheter. He was somnolent on admission, with urine toxicology positive for cocaine, opiates, and benzodiazepines, contributing to altered mental status. He was treated with IV cefepime, later transitioned to oral cefpodoxime after urine cultures grew E. coli and Klebsiella. A fungal infection of the scrotal area was diagnosed and treated with topical miconazole. On hospital day four, he developed nausea and vomiting with elevated amylase and lipase, leading to a diagnosis of possible pancreatitis, likely related to medications or hypertriglyceridemia; symptoms resolved with supportive care. Constipation was managed with suppositories and enema. His kidney function improved with hydration. Alprazolam was discontinued due to substance use concerns. He was discharged home with follow-up in GI, nephrology, and primary care, with clear instructions on medication changes and symptom monitoring.
